newsitem.title: USA: Tarantino, Madonna in record label deal.
newsitem.headline: Tarantino, Madonna in record label deal.

text.p: Movie director Quentin Tarantino and pop star Madonna have joined forces to muscle in on the music business, they announced Thursday.
Together with his producing partner Lawrence Bender, Tarantino has formed A Band Apart Records, whose releases will be marketed and distributed by Madonna's Maverick Records.
"The potential is truly extraordinary," Madonna said in a statement issued through the filmmakers' representatives at the William Morris Agency.

The imprint will focus on soundtracks, and its inaugural release will be the soundtrack to Tarantino's next movie "Jackie Brown," both of which are scheduled for release at Christmas. The film noir's ensemble cast includes Robert De Niro, Pam Grier, Samuel L. Jackson and Bridget Fonda.
The soundtracks for Tarantino's two previous films, "Reservoir Dogs" and "Pulp Fiction" were both strong sellers for MCA Records, a unit of Seagram Co. Ltd..
In fact the Maverick deal brings Tarantino full-circle to "Reservoir Dogs," whose opening scene depicted gangsters in a scholarly discussion of Madonna's songs.

Maverick, which is distributed by Time Warner Inc's Warner Bros. Records, handles such artists as Alanis Morissette and Prodigy. Tarantino shared the 1994 original screenplay Oscar for "Pulp Fiction" with Roger Avary.
